# Codex hooks reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_hooks_reference.py. Do not edit manually. -->

This reference covers all 11 hook events and all 21 committed command schema fixtures in `codex-rs/hooks/schema/generated/`. Field tables and raw schemas come directly from those fixtures; lifecycle and operational details are traced to the Rust sources named throughout the document.

The schemas describe accepted wire shapes. The runtime may intentionally support only a subset of schema-reserved decisions; those restrictions are called out below.

| Event | Fires | Matcher input | Scope | Output schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`SessionStart`](#session-start) | Before the first model turn after startup, resume, clear, or compaction. | Session source: `startup`, `resume`, `clear`, or `compact`. | `thread` | `session-start.command.output.schema.json` |
| [`SessionEnd`](#session-end) | During root-session teardown, after Codex attempts to flush the transcript. | Fixed reason `other`. | `thread` | none |

## Availability and configuration

The feature key is `features.hooks` (stage `Stable`, default `true`). The legacy feature alias `features.codex_hooks` resolves to the same feature. Guardian review sessions disable hooks even when their parent session enables them.

Hooks can be declared under `[hooks]` in a config layer or in a sibling `hooks.json`. The JSON wrapper accepts an optional `description` plus a `hooks` object. If both representations contain hooks for the same layer, Codex loads both and emits a warning.

```toml
[features]
hooks = true

[[hooks.PreToolUse]]
matcher = '^(Bash|apply_patch)$'

[[hooks.PreToolUse.hooks]]
type = "command"
command = "python3 .codex/hooks/pre_tool.py"
commandWindows = "python .codex\\hooks\\pre_tool.py"
timeout = 30
statusMessage = "Checking policy"
additionalContextLimit = 2500

[hooks.state.'C:\path\to\.codex\hooks.json:pre_tool_use:0:0']
enabled = true
trusted_hash = "<hash returned by hooks/list>"
```

Configured handler variants are `command`, `prompt`, `agent`. Only `command` executes today; `prompt` and `agent` parse successfully but discovery skips them with warnings. Empty commands are also skipped. `commandWindows` overrides `command` only on Windows.

| Command field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `command` | Shell command used on non-Windows platforms and as the Windows fallback. |
| `commandWindows` | Optional Windows-only command override; `command_windows` is accepted as an alias. |
| `timeout` | Seconds; defaults to 600, is normalized to at least 1, with a stricter SessionEnd rule below. |
| `async` | Unsupported. Non-SessionEnd async hooks are skipped; SessionEnd emits a warning and still runs synchronously. |
| `statusMessage` | Optional UI text carried in running/completed summaries. |
| `additionalContextLimit` | Approximate per-handler token spill threshold; absent uses 2,500, `0` disables spilling. Valid only for context-producing events. |

Hook state keys use `<source>:<snake_case_event>:<matcher_group_index>:<handler_index>`. The positional suffix is not yet a durable hook ID. Only user and session-flag layers may set `enabled` and `trusted_hash`; later layers win field by field.

## Discovery, trust, matching, and execution

### Discovery and trust

1. Managed requirements hooks are appended first. Across requirement layers, event lists are append-only; conflicting active-platform managed directories fail closed.
2. Active config layers are visited from lowest to highest precedence. Each unique layer folder may contribute `hooks.json`, followed by the layer's TOML hooks.
3. Plugin hook sources are appended last. Plugin commands receive `PLUGIN_ROOT`, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`, `PLUGIN_DATA`, and `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA`; `${NAME}` placeholders for these variables are expanded before execution.
4. `allow_managed_hooks_only` filters every unmanaged source, including user, project, session-flag, and plugin hooks. Managed hooks are always enabled and have trust status `managed`.

Unmanaged commands are hashed from a normalized event/matcher/handler identity. A matching stored hash is `trusted`; a different stored hash is `modified`; no stored hash is `untrusted`. Only enabled managed/trusted hooks execute, unless the invocation uses `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`. Bypass does not re-enable an explicitly disabled hook.

### Matcher rules

An omitted matcher, `""`, or `"*"` matches all. A pattern containing only ASCII letters, digits, `_`, and `|` is an exact-name list; other patterns compile as Rust regular expressions. Invalid regexes skip the entire matcher group with a warning. `UserPromptSubmit` and `Stop` discard configured matchers. Tool events also test internal compatibility aliases, but each handler runs at most once and stdin always retains the canonical tool name (`apply_patch` also matches `Write`/`Edit`; `spawn_agent` also matches `Agent`).

### Command protocol and scheduling

Every selected command receives one compact JSON object on stdin (no trailing newline), runs with the event `cwd`, and has piped stdin/stdout/stderr. On Windows the fallback is `%COMSPEC% /C`; elsewhere it is `$SHELL -lc`. A connected execution environment may supply its own derived shell program/arguments. Output bytes are decoded lossily as UTF-8, and the child is configured to be killed if its future is dropped.

All matching handlers for one event start concurrently. Results are collected by completion but sorted back into configured/display order for reporting and most aggregation. The one intentional completion-order rule is competing `PreToolUse.updatedInput`: the last process to finish wins. Duplicate declarations are not deduplicated.

| Timeout class | Default | Bound |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Most command hooks | 600s | minimum 1s; no explicit maximum |
| `SessionEnd` | 1s | 1–3s |

Spawn, stdin-write, wait, timeout, missing-exit-code, serialization, and nonzero-exit errors are recorded as failed hook runs; they do not by themselves abort unrelated matching handlers. Exit code `0` enables event-specific stdout parsing. Exit code `2` is a special block/deny signal only for `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, `PostToolUse`, `SubagentStop`, and `Stop`, and requires a non-empty stderr reason.

## Output protocol, context limits, and observability

A successful JSON response must be exactly one JSON object. Unknown fields are rejected by the generated command schemas. Universal fields are `continue` (default `true`), `stopReason`, `suppressOutput` (default `false`), and `systemMessage`. Event parsers apply stricter semantic rules than the schemas: for example, `PreToolUse` and `PermissionRequest` reject `continue:false`, `stopReason`, and `suppressOutput`; `PostToolUse` rejects `suppressOutput`. `systemMessage` becomes a warning entry. Several events currently parse but otherwise ignore `suppressOutput`.

`additionalContext` is supported only by `SessionStart`, `SubagentStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, and `PostToolUse`. Each original context is compared with an approximate 2,500-token default. Oversized text is saved in full below `<OS temp>/hook_outputs/<thread_id>/<uuid>.txt` and replaced by a budgeted head/tail preview plus the recovery path. A write failure falls back to an in-memory truncated preview. `additionalContextLimit = 0` disables spilling for that handler.

Codex emits `hook/started` and `hook/completed` app-server v2 notifications. Run summaries include ID, event, handler/execution type, scope, source/path, display order, status message, timestamps, duration, status, and typed entries (`warning`, `stop`, `feedback`, `context`, or `error`). `hooks/list` resolves effective hook metadata, warnings, and errors for each cwd, including enablement, current hash, trust status, plugin ID, and configured context limit. Completed runs also emit count/duration metrics and analytics tagged by event, source, and status. Hook started/completed events are not reconstructed into thread history.

### Legacy `notify` hook

Top-level `notify = [program, args...]` is separate from the 11 configurable command events. After an agent turn, Codex appends one kebab-case JSON argument with type `agent-turn-complete`, thread/turn IDs, cwd, optional client, input messages, and the last assistant message. It uses null stdio, does not wait for completion, and a spawn failure is logged while the turn continues.

## SessionStart

- Timing: Before the first model turn after startup, resume, clear, or compaction.
- Matcher: Session source: `startup`, `resume`, `clear`, or `compact`.
- Scope: `thread`.
- Plain stdout on exit 0: Injected as additional model context.
- Exit code 2: Failure; no special exit-code-2 behavior.
- Aggregation: Any `continue:false` stops startup; contexts remain in declaration order.
- `continue:false` stops a root session start and may carry `stopReason`.
- `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` and non-JSON stdout become contextual user fragments.
- A JSON-looking but invalid payload fails the hook; empty stdout is a successful no-op.
- Runtime source: `codex-rs/hooks/src/events/session_start.rs`.

## SessionEnd

- Timing: During root-session teardown, after Codex attempts to flush the transcript.
- Matcher: Fixed reason `other`.
- Scope: `thread`.
- Plain stdout on exit 0: Ignored.
- Exit code 2: Failure; no special exit-code-2 behavior.
- Aggregation: Every matched process is awaited; output cannot change teardown.
- Runs only for root sessions; thread-spawn subagents use `SubagentStart`/`SubagentStop`.
- Has an input schema but intentionally no command output schema.
- Defaults to a 1-second timeout and is capped at 3 seconds to preserve shutdown headroom.
- Runtime source: `codex-rs/hooks/src/events/session_end.rs`.

### SessionEnd command output

`SessionEnd` does not declare a command output schema. Stdout is ignored; only process completion, timeout/error state, exit code, and stderr on failure affect the run summary.

## UserPromptSubmit

- Timing: Before a user input is recorded and submitted to the model.
- Matcher: Ignored; every handler for the event runs.
- Scope: `turn`.
- Plain stdout on exit 0: Injected as additional model context.
- Exit code 2: Blocks submission when stderr contains a reason.
- Aggregation: Any stop/block stops submission; first reason wins; contexts preserve declaration order.
- Supports `continue:false`, `decision:block`, and `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`.
- A block decision requires a non-empty `reason`; context emitted with a valid block is retained.
- Plain stdout is context, while JSON-looking invalid stdout fails the hook.
- Runtime source: `codex-rs/hooks/src/events/user_prompt_submit.rs`.

## PreToolUse

- Timing: Immediately before a selected tool handler executes.
- Matcher: Canonical tool name plus compatibility aliases.
- Scope: `turn`.
- Plain stdout on exit 0: Ignored unless it looks like invalid JSON.
- Exit code 2: Blocks the tool call when stderr contains a reason.
- Aggregation: Any deny blocks; first block reason wins; last-completing valid input rewrite wins.
- Supports legacy `decision:block` and hook-specific `permissionDecision:deny`.
- `permissionDecision:allow` is accepted only with `updatedInput`; `ask` is unsupported.
- A block discards every proposed input rewrite; additional context remains available.
- Runtime source: `codex-rs/hooks/src/events/pre_tool_use.rs`.

## PermissionRequest

- Timing: In the approval path before guardian review or user approval UI.
- Matcher: Canonical tool name plus compatibility aliases.
- Scope: `turn`.
- Plain stdout on exit 0: Ignored unless it looks like invalid JSON.
- Exit code 2: Denies approval when stderr contains a reason.
- Aggregation: Any deny wins; otherwise the last applicable allow wins; no verdict defers to normal approval.
- Returns an optional allow/deny verdict and never rewrites tool input.
- `updatedInput`, `updatedPermissions`, and `interrupt:true` are reserved but unsupported.
- The approval path budgets the maximum matching hook timeout because handlers run concurrently.
- Runtime source: `codex-rs/hooks/src/events/permission_request.rs`.

## PostToolUse

- Timing: After a tool has produced a successful output.
- Matcher: Canonical tool name plus compatibility aliases.
- Scope: `turn`.
- Plain stdout on exit 0: Ignored unless it looks like invalid JSON.
- Exit code 2: Blocks follow-up processing and feeds stderr back to the model.
- Aggregation: Any explicit block wins; feedback and additional context preserve declaration order.
- `continue:false` marks the hook stopped and substitutes feedback for the model-visible tool output; the tool has already run.
- `decision:block` rejects the completed tool result back to the model but cannot undo its side effects.
- A block requires a non-empty reason; `updatedMCPToolOutput` is unsupported.
- Stop/block feedback is joined with blank lines and may be spilled before model visibility.
- Runtime source: `codex-rs/hooks/src/events/post_tool_use.rs`.

## PreCompact

- Timing: Immediately before manual or automatic context compaction.
- Matcher: Compaction trigger: `manual` or `auto`.
- Scope: `turn`.
- Plain stdout on exit 0: Ignored unless it looks like invalid JSON.
- Exit code 2: Failure; stderr is used as the error message.
- Aggregation: Any `continue:false` prevents compaction; first stop reason wins.
- Only the universal output fields are declared.
- `continue:false` stops before compaction; a missing reason gets a synthesized status message.
- Block decisions and plain-text context are not part of this event contract.
- Runtime source: `codex-rs/hooks/src/events/compact.rs`.

## PostCompact

- Timing: After manual or automatic context compaction completes.
- Matcher: Compaction trigger: `manual` or `auto`.
- Scope: `turn`.
- Plain stdout on exit 0: Ignored unless it looks like invalid JSON.
- Exit code 2: Failure; stderr is used as the error message.
- Aggregation: Any `continue:false` stops the post-compaction flow; first stop reason wins.
- Only the universal output fields are declared.
- Compaction has already happened when this event runs.
- Block decisions and plain-text context are not part of this event contract.
- Runtime source: `codex-rs/hooks/src/events/compact.rs`.

## SubagentStart

- Timing: When a user-visible thread-spawn subagent starts.
- Matcher: Subagent `agent_type`.
- Scope: `thread`.
- Plain stdout on exit 0: Injected as additional model context.
- Exit code 2: Failure; no special exit-code-2 behavior.
- Aggregation: Contexts preserve declaration order; stop decisions are ignored.
- Shares start-hook output handling but is context-injection-only.
- `continue:false` is parsed but does not stop a subagent start.
- Internal or synthetic subagents do not expose user-configured lifecycle hooks.
- Runtime source: `codex-rs/hooks/src/events/session_start.rs`.

## SubagentStop

- Timing: When a user-visible thread-spawn subagent reaches turn completion.
- Matcher: Subagent `agent_type`.
- Scope: `turn`.
- Plain stdout on exit 0: Invalid; successful output must be JSON or empty.
- Exit code 2: Blocks completion and uses stderr as a continuation prompt.
- Aggregation: Any `continue:false` overrides blocks; otherwise all blocking prompts are preserved.
- Includes parent and subagent transcript paths when available.
- `decision:block` produces a hook-attributed continuation fragment for the subagent.
- Blocking fragments are model-budgeted and may spill to the OS temporary directory.
- Runtime source: `codex-rs/hooks/src/events/stop.rs`.

## Stop

- Timing: After a root agent turn reaches completion, before completion is finalized.
- Matcher: Ignored; every handler for the event runs.
- Scope: `turn`.
- Plain stdout on exit 0: Invalid; successful output must be JSON or empty.
- Exit code 2: Blocks completion and uses stderr as a continuation prompt.
- Aggregation: Any `continue:false` overrides blocks; otherwise blocking reasons are joined in declaration order.
- `decision:block` asks the agent to continue with the supplied reason.
- `stop_hook_active` lets a hook detect a continuation caused by an earlier Stop hook.
- Blocking prompts retain per-hook attribution and may spill before model injection.
- Runtime source: `codex-rs/hooks/src/events/stop.rs`.

## Canonical source map

- `codex-rs/config/src/hook_config.rs`: config and handler shapes.
- `codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/discovery.rs`: sources, precedence, normalization, trust, and enablement.
- `codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/dispatcher.rs`: matching, concurrency, ordering, summaries, and scopes.
- `codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/command_runner.rs`: shell, stdin/stdout/stderr, timeout, and process behavior.
- `codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/output_parser.rs`: JSON decisions and unsupported combinations.
- `codex-rs/hooks/src/events/*.rs`: per-event timing inputs, exit semantics, and aggregation.
- `codex-rs/core/src/hook_runtime.rs`: integration into turns, tools, approvals, compaction, and subagents.
- `codex-rs/hooks/src/output_spill.rs`: model-visible context budget and spill files.
- `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/hook.rs` and `plugin.rs`: public notifications and catalog metadata.
- `codex-rs/hooks/src/legacy_notify.rs`: legacy post-turn notification compatibility.
